title: Workflow Templates: Free Options Compared (2026 Guide)
summary: Workflow templates differ in size, features, and integration options across six automation platforms. Compare the libraries to find your best fit.
body_markdown:
## 3. Activepieces: best for free, editable, self-hostable templates


After that complaint, Activepieces fits, because you can run its templates on your own server, where loops and routers cost whatever your hardware costs, not a metered operation each.


> Operation-based billing also punishes loops and routers, the very features its templates showcase.


For small teams and developers who want to edit every step of a template and choose where it runs, Activepieces lets you open, change and self-host every flow across its 740 integrations, with **unlimited flows on every plan** , including free, so you may need custom integrations.


The core is MIT-licensed, while some enterprise features sit under a separate commercial licence.


There's a free cloud tier, and you can self-host the community edition at no licence cost. I'm not quoting the cloud limits here. Read them on the pricing page against your own monthly run count before you commit, because that's where any per-run math breaks.


### Template: form response to Sheets and Slack


The trigger is a new Google Forms response. Every step stays editable. It receives the response through[Google Forms](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-forms) , appends a row to a spreadsheet in[Google Sheets](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-sheets) , then posts a summary to a channel in[Slack](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/slack) , the team chat tool.


Start this flow free in Activepieces:[https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up](https://cloud.activepieces.com/sign-up?ap_cta=blog_body&ref=%2Fblog%2Fworkflow-templates-free-options-compared-2026-guide)


### Template: Stripe payment to invoice and bookkeeping


When a payment succeeds in[Stripe](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/stripe) , the payment processor, the flow creates an invoice record in[QuickBooks](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/quickbooks) , the accounting package, and logs the sale in Google Sheets. Add a branch for failed payments, and you're paying for a router only on a metered platform.


You can edit every step, inspect the code behind each integration (all 740 sit in the open source monorepo on GitHub, roughly 60% of them community-contributed), and move the same flow between cloud and your own server, so you're not waiting on the vendor's roadmap to connect tools you need.


Nobody has to take a sales call to learn what self-hosting costs.


Most vendors strip the self-hosted build to sell control separately, so the question is whether moving a template onto your own server costs you the governance features.


It doesn't: the air-gapped build carries the same single sign-on, user provisioning, custom roles, audit trail, release management and secrets-manager support as the managed cloud, which can be pinned to an EU or US region and holds SOC 2 Type II.


MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run Activepieces in production.


Once you self-host, uptime, upgrades and backups are yours. Its app catalogue is smaller than Zapier's or Make's, so check that your apps exist first.


If you need the widest catalogue, pick Zapier. If you want heavy visual data handling, Make. If you want maximum code-level control, n8n.
